text:
sarah: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — thanks for the roadmap clarity. A few concrete process questions bubbled up in eng: what's the recommended cadence to minimize oncall thrash? And can leadership clarify quality bars / SLAs distinction between Hosted and Dedicated? I'm collecting answers for the handbook.

mike: TL;DR: favor smaller, predictable releases and instrumented rollouts. Dedicated has stricter QA & SLOs. I'll spell out numbers below.

julia: Practically: daily commits are fine, but schedule production-facing deploy windows (e.g., Tue/Thu afternoons) to reduce surprises. Use feature flags + staged canaries for infra/runtime changes.

devon: Can we get a short rollout checklist we can paste in teams' runbooks? 

julia: Sure. Typical staged rollout we use:
``n1) internal smoke on single instance
2) 10% cross-region canary (30m monitor)
3) 50% traffic split (15m monitor + perf checks)
4) full rollout
5) post-rollout smoke + metrics check
```
Always have an explicit rollback plan at each step.

rajiv: Ops proposal question: are we changing oncall windows? I saw a draft with mixed 24/12 coverage. What's final?

sarah: We agreed to keep a 24h primary coverage but trial a 12h floater for daytime high-traffic windows to reduce fatigue. Emily will post the rotation grid. Trial length: 6 weeks.

emily: Rotation excerpt from ops doc:
``n- Primary: 24h team coverage (Mon-Sun)
- Floater: 12h (08:00-20:00 PST) for peak overlaps
- Weekends: 3-person compressed pools
```
We'll report back metrics on pager volume and MTTR.

anita: From product: Dedicated SLA targets we're proposing — 99.9% regional inference availability; 99.5% for control-plane ops. We'll publish the draft in the partner portal for feedback.

mike: Engineering-level quality bars: release blocks if any of: failing end-to-end smoke, >2 critical SLO regressions, security vulnerability. Post-deploy validation windows: 30m for infra/model changes; 15m for pure app code.

rajiv: What incident thresholds should trigger immediate rollback vs mitigation? E.g., sustained latency spike or error-rate jump.

julia: The thresholds we plan to codify: 
``n- Latency: >3x P50 baseline sustained >5 minutes -> rollback
- Error rate: +0.5% absolute increase sustained >3 minutes -> rollback
- GPU/CPU saturation: >90% sustained >10 minutes -> degrade non-critical workloads
```
We'll put these into the release playbook with monitoring alerts wired to the deploy pipeline.

devon: I'll volunteer to draft the release playbook. Need reviewers from SRE and Product.

sarah: Great — ask Emily and Rajiv for SRE review, Anita for product sign-off. Devon, can you target a draft by next Tuesday?

devon: Yes, drafting now. Target: next Tue.

ci-cd-bot: nightly-e2e passed; canary image pushed to staging (img: rwd/inference:staging-2026-03-01).

mike: Note on Dedicated rollouts: avoid pairing quantization/kernel changes with weight updates in the same release unless you have local perf/regression benches and QA signoff. That combo has caused incidents before.

anita: Also, for Dedicated customers we'll give >=48h advance-notice for major infra or model-impacting changes. Account teams will coordinate.

sarah: Action items I'll track:
- Devon: own first draft of release playbook (ops + product reviewers) — due Tue
- Julia/Mike: add rollback thresholds + monitoring hooks to playbook
- Emily: begin 6-week rotation trial and report cadence/MTTR impact
- Anita: publish Dedicated SLA draft to partner portal
I'll post the consolidated doc link here when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

emily: Recording + slides: https://redwood.company/all-hands/2026-03-01

rajiv: Small ask: add a postmortem template (owners, timeline, comms plan) to the playbook so incident response is consistent.

sarah: Yes — include that in the draft, Rajiv. I'll track reviewers.

mike: If teams need exception windows for large rollouts, file requests in #release-war-room with impact analysis.

sarah: Closing this thread — will ping when the draft is live. Thanks everyone!
